candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XXV.2 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

'Let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them' — Ephrem reads this verse as the canonical warrant for every consecrated dwelling-place of God: the tabernacle prefigures the Incarnation ('the Word was made flesh and tabernacled among us,' Jn 1:14), and the Incarnation prefigures the Church. Tewahedo cites Ex 25:8 as the principal canonical anchor of its tabot tradition — the Ark-as-sanctuary at the center of every Tewahedo church.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XXV.9 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Two cherubim of gold beaten out of one piece, their wings stretched over the mercy seat, are for Ephrem the canonical sign that the divine throne rests over a place of propitiation, not over a tribunal alone. The mercy seat between the wings is the OT type of the Cross where mercy meets the Law. Tewahedo iconography preserves the cherub-flanked tabot in every sanctuary.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Two cherubim of gold beaten out of one piece, their wings stretched over the mercy seat, are for Ephrem the canonical sign that the divine throne rests over a place of propitiation, not over a tribunal alone. The mercy seat between the wings is the OT type of the Cross where mercy meets the Law. Tewahedo iconography preserves the cherub-flanked tabot in every sanctuary.

Tewahedo cites Ex 25:8 as the principal canonical anchor of its tabot tradition — the Ark-as-sanctuary at the center of every Tewahedo church.
